feature_candidates.description: Inverse or log-transformed rank of the video within the user's impression request, added as an input feature.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Captures exposure-order bias; earlier positions likely have higher long_view probability, improving ranking within each user.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Extract position from impression log order or request_id; add as scalar embedding or bias term in model input.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low if position is independent of label; verify with train-only analysis that ordering is not by relevance.
feature_candidates.name: position_rank_decay

feature_candidates.description: Learnable per-tab bias scalar added to the scoring function, applied uniformly within a user's impressions.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Normalizes strong tab-level long_view rate differences, allowing ranking across heterogeneous tabs.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Map tab integer to a trainable embedding or bias vector; add to logit before final score.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low; tab is an observed context, but must be validated on train-only to avoid overfitting to distribution shifts.
feature_candidates.name: tab_bias_term

feature_candidates.description: Per-user historical count of long_view or click on each video_id, computed strictly from the training period.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Captures repeat-view tendency and familiarity, which static features cannot represent.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Aggregate train-log rows by (user, video) before any validation; feed as an extra numeric feature.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: High if computed on train+valid; must use train-only history and strict temporal split to avoid validation label leakage.
feature_candidates.name: user_video_interaction_count

findings.evidence: DATA CARD Tab Breakdown: tab 0 rate 4.22%, tab 4 rate 48.93%, tab 1 rate 38.61%.
findings.implication: Within-user ranking may need tab-specific bias terms or conditional normalization to avoid overfitting to tab distribution shifts.
findings.observation: Long_view rate ranges from 4.22% (tab 0) to 48.93% (tab 4) versus 38.61% for tab 1; tab 0 holds 13.15% of rows.
findings.title: Tab dominates long_view rate variation

findings.implication: Any popularity feature derived from them must be treated as leaky and only used for hypothesis testing, not as a production feature.
findings.observation: Video statistics aggregate full-platform traffic (12.83B shows vs 2.62M logged, ratio ~4892:1) and span periods 45-181 days beyond the log.
findings.title: Video statistics are heavily leakage-prone

findings.evidence: EXPERIMENT history shows bpr_b03 with primary 0.6040; no history_features or position inputs were used.
findings.implication: Position-aware bias and train-only user-video counts (history_features family) could capture repeat-view tendency and exposure-order effects.
findings.observation: Current BPR experiments only use static features and user/item IDs; no position or per-user interaction counts are tested.
findings.title: Position and user-video history are underrepresented

expected_artifacts: A correlation/conditional-rate table: long_view rate by tab, hour window, and position percentile (train-only).
A user-video interaction count feature test (train-only) compared against baseline bpr in a single experiment.
A monotonic gain plot showing how long_view rate changes with log video-statistic counts, split by tab.
A short EDA report listing the top 3 feature hypotheses prioritized for the next model experiment.
feature_hypotheses: Position-aware bias: add the rank of the video within the user's impression request (or derived inverse position) as an input feature, since earlier positions often have higher long_view probability.
Tab-specific conditional bias: include tab as an input bias term that scales a learned per-tab baseline, potentially improving ranking within dominated tabs.
User-video interaction counts: compute per-user historical long_view or click counts on each video_id (train-period only) and feed as a history_features family input, capturing repeat-view tendency.

Video popularity monotonic features: convert leaky video statistics into monotonic buckets or log-transformed counts and test them under history_features as a low-risk feature family, with explicit leakage caveat.
leakage_risks: Video statistics are period aggregates over full-platform traffic (12.83B shows vs 2.62M logged), so they leak future and unrelated exposure information; must be caveated and only used to test hypotheses, never to guide production.
Computing per-user historical counts on train+valid combined would leak validation labels into training; use train-only history or ensure a strict temporal split.
Position features may directly encode label leakage if the log already sorts by relevance or if position is derived from ranking; verify position is independent of the label.
Tab is a strong confound with label rate (tab 4: 48.9% long_view vs tab 0: 4.2%), so any tab-derived bias must be validated only on train to avoid overfitting to tab distribution shifts.
plan.objective: Run a leakage-safe EDA pass on train+valid KuaiRand-Pure logs to identify reusable, registered-family feature hypotheses that can improve within-user long_view ranking (GAUC, nDCG@5) beyond the current best primary 0.6040.
questions: Within each user's tab and request context, how does the position (rank) of a video in the impression list correlate with long_view, after controlling for tab and hour?
Which tab subgroups have the highest long_view lift relative to tab-1 baseline, and does ranking within those tabs need separate normalization or bias terms?

What is the per-user distribution of video type / upload_type / author_id interactions, and are there user groups with systematic long_view preference differences over these categorical video features?

Do count-based video statistics (e.g., play_cnt, like_cnt) exhibit a monotonically increasing relationship with long_view within a user's impressions, and is that relationship stable across tabs and hours?
required_inputs: Train and validation interaction logs (user, item, tab, position/request_id, timestamp, and all label columns).
User profile table and video feature table (100% coverage).
Video statistics table (period aggregate) with clear leakage flag.
Existing feature extraction pipeline or method card for bpr, group_softmax, history_features, multi_task families.

report.recommended_next_focus: Run a train-only EDA to measure conditional long_view rate by position percentile and tab; then add the position_rank_decay and tab_bias_term features to BPR in a single experiment to test their combined uplift.
report.summary: EDA passes on the KuaiRand-Pure log identify tab, position, and train-only user-video history as the highest-priority feature families for improving within-user long_view ranking. Tab shows strong label-rate variation (38.6% tab1 vs 4.2% tab0), and the leaky video-statistics table is unsuitable for production features. Recommended experiment: add position and tab bias terms under bpr, then test train-only interaction counts.
